messages:
maria_cs: Quick help — we're kicking off ACME enterprise onboarding next week. Need a short preflight runbook (customer-facing) covering caching/batching/streaming best-practices + renewal-risk mitigations. Can we assemble something lightweight we can hand to their SREs and PMs? :wave:

sam_solutions: Yes. I can draft a 1-page checklist. Key pieces: expected traffic profile, pad warmup plan, KV cache priming, batching window guidance, streaming fallbacks. Also call out quota/latency targets and renewal signal thresholds.

eli_eng: For warmup I recommend a 3-stage approach: 1) model ping (small inference) 2) prefix priming (top 50 user prompts) 3) sustained low qps ramp to target. Use our warmup endpoint: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/warmup -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"endpoint":"/v1/generate","batch_size":1}'
```

zoe_ops: Add the autoscale thresholds: scale-up at 60% GPU util, burst policy for 10m at +30% cap, and enable overprovision for first 48h of live. Alerting: latency p50>350ms or error_rate>0.5% => page oncall.

sam_solutions: For caching: recommend prefix caching for predictable prompts (login flows, canned replies). Provide example TTLs: ephemeral session KV: 30m, conversation-level prefix: 24h, long-tail template cache: 7d. Note: don't cache personal data.

eli_eng: On batching: use a max batch latency of 45ms for latency-sensitive routes, and 200ms for throughput routes. Client-side guidance: buffer up to 8 requests or 20ms whichever comes first. Server-side: enable adaptive batching and per-route batch cap.

maria_cs: What about streaming? customers often ask how to preserve UX while using batching.

eli_eng: Recommend hybrid streaming: stream first token as soon as available, then flush batched tokens every 50ms. If you need deterministic ordering, use request IDs and assemble on client. Also provide fallback to non-streaming if connection drops.

sam_solutions: Renewal risk signals to include in runbook: low weekly active users (<10% of projected), sustained latency regressions, repeated rate limit hits, lack of feature adoption. Recommend 14-day enablement checkpoints and a 'red flag' playbook for CS (stakeholder escalation, prioritized remediation, usage incentives).

zoe_ops: For feedback capture: add a short in-app survey post-integration and attach a 10-prompt eval set we can run nightly. Use tag 'onboard-acme-2026' in eval dashboard. Route qualitative feedback to the customer thread in Zendesk and tag in Salesforce.

sam_solutions: Quick operational snippets to hand to SREs:

KV priming example:

```json
{"action":"prime_kv","keys":["session:template:v1","onboard:top50"],"ttl_secs":86400}
```

Warmup rollout plan (suggested):
- Day 0: internal smoke + prefix priming
- Day 1: 10% prod traffic for 2h, monitor p50/p95 and errors
- Day 2: 50% prod traffic for 4h if stable
- Day 3+: full traffic with overprovision for 48h

eli_eng: Also include a minimal client snippet for graceful streaming assembly:

```js
// client: collect chunks with request_id then assemble
fetch('/v1/stream', {method:'POST'}).then(s=>{
  // stream handler collects partials
})
```

maria_cs: Nice. Can one of you assemble a 1-page PDF and a single Slack message we can send to ACME SRE/PM? Need it by EOD tomorrow.

sam_solutions: I'll assemble the PDF and draft the Slack message. Will attach warmup script and a minimal curl snippet.

eli_eng: I'll include the KV priming script, batch/stream params, and a short rollback checklist.

deploy-bot: Reminder: Dedicated pool for acme-prod scheduled for 2026-03-02 10:00 UTC. Autoscale enabled.

maria_cs: Great — thanks all. If anyone has an existing internal runbook link drop it here. :thumbsup:
